lessons.title: What Is in Space?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name the sun, moon, and at least one planet.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a picture of the night sky.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss the sun, moon, stars, and planets using pictures/simple models.
resources_needed: Space picture cards, simple solar system model
key_questions: What can you see in the night sky?

differentiation.support: Focus on sun, moon, and one planet (Earth)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of space vocabulary — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap what we know about space.
lessons.home_link: Look at the night sky together and talk about what you see.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Whatever Next!' by Jill Murphy
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe Baby Bear's imaginative space journey.
lessons.main_activity: Read the story, discussing Baby Bear's imaginative adventure to the moon using everyday objects.
key_questions: What did Baby Bear use as a rocket?
What did he find on the moon?

differentiation.extension: Explain the imaginative elements of the story

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and imaginative understanding — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.home_link: Imagine your own space adventure and share it with family.

lessons.title: Rocket Countdown: Counting Backwards from 10
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count backwards from 10 to 1.
lessons.main_activity: Children practise counting backwards from 10 with a 'rocket launch' action game, extending the range from Week 10.
key_questions: What comes after 7 when counting backwards?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note backward counting range progress — evidence for MATHS.1.

lessons.title: Making a Rocket Craft
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a rocket model using recycled materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at picture examples of rockets.
lessons.main_activity: Children build a rocket using a cardboard tube, cone, and craft materials, decorating with their own design.
resources_needed: Cardboard tubes, card cones, craft materials, paint
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe construction planning and material joining skill — evidence for EAD.1.
lessons.plenary: Display rockets together as a 'launch pad'.
lessons.home_link: Build a rocket using recycling at home.

lessons.title: Day and Night: The Earth and Sun
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain simply why we have day and night.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what happens as it gets dark.
lessons.main_activity: Using a torch (sun) and globe/ball (Earth), demonstrate simply how the Earth spinning creates day and night.
key_questions: Why does it get dark at night?

differentiation.support: Watch the demonstration and describe what they see
differentiation.extension: Explain the concept in their own words

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early understanding of Earth's rotation — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap why we have day and night.
lessons.home_link: Notice when it gets light/dark and talk about why with family.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'th' Digraph
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the digraph sound 'th' and blend words (this, that, thin).
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'th' digraph sound/action; blend new words.
key_questions: What sound do these two letters make?

lessons.title: Ordering Planets by Size
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to order planet pictures by size.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of planets of different sizes.
lessons.main_activity: Children order planet picture cutouts from smallest to biggest, using comparative language.
resources_needed: Planet picture cutouts of varying sizes
lessons.assessment_notes: Note size-ordering skill — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of planet size order.
lessons.home_link: Order objects at home by size.

lessons.title: Astronaut Movement in Space
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move imaginatively as if floating in zero gravity.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what happens to astronauts in space (floating).
lessons.main_activity: Children move in slow motion around the space pretending to float like astronauts, exploring imaginative movement.
key_questions: How does an astronaut move in space?
Can you move in slow motion?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative and controlled movement — evidence for EAD.2/PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss how it felt to move like an astronaut.
lessons.home_link: Move in slow motion together at home like astronauts.

lessons.title: Famous Astronauts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name a famous astronaut and something they did.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what an astronaut's job involves.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce a famous astronaut (e.g. Neil Armstrong, Tim Peake) with simple facts about their achievements.
key_questions: Would you like to be an astronaut? Why?

differentiation.support: Share one simple fact with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note factual recall about a real person from the past — evidence for UTW.1/UTW.2.
lessons.home_link: Look up a famous astronaut together.

lessons.title: Writing Space Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write simple space-themed words.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sounds learned including new digraphs.
lessons.main_activity: Children write/draw simple space words (moon, star, sun) using known phonics sounds.
key_questions: What space word will you write?
What sound does it start with?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share space word pictures with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Write a space word together at home.

lessons.title: Counting Stars
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count star stickers/counters accurately up to 10+.
lessons.starter_activity: Count stars on a night sky picture together.
lessons.main_activity: Children count and place a given number of star stickers onto a 'night sky' picture, checking accuracy.
key_questions: Can you count them again to check?

differentiation.extension: Count to 10+ and compare with a partner

lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.home_link: Count stars in the sky together in the evening if possible.

lessons.title: How Do Rockets Launch?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe simply how a rocket launches (fuel, force, upward).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the countdown activity from Monday.
lessons.main_activity: (If resources allow) demonstrate a simple balloon or film canister 'rocket' launch, discussing the force that pushes it up.
resources_needed: Balloon rocket or film canister/effervescent tablet experiment materials

differentiation.support: Watch the demonstration and describe what happened
differentiation.extension: Predict what will happen before the launch

lessons.assessment_notes: Note investigative observation of force and movement — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap what makes a rocket launch.
lessons.home_link: Blow up a balloon and let it go to see it 'launch' at home.

lessons.title: Retelling 'Whatever Next!'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the story's key events in sequence.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards, children retell the story sequence using sequencing words and props.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group retells to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Shapes in a Rocket Design
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify and name 2D shapes used in a rocket design.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at Monday's rocket craft and identify shapes used.
lessons.main_activity: Children design a rocket on paper using given 2D shape stencils, naming each shape used.
key_questions: What shape is the rocket's body?

differentiation.extension: Combine 4+ shapes and name them all

lessons.assessment_notes: Note shape recognition and application — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.home_link: Look for shapes in objects around your home.

lessons.title: Space Song and Dance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sing a space-themed song with actions.
lessons.main_activity: Learn a simple space-themed song with actions (rocket launch, floating, twinkling stars), performing with confidence.
key_questions: What action goes with this line?
Which part of space do you like moving as most?

differentiation.extension: Suggest and lead a new action

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe participation and expressive movement — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.home_link: Sing the space song for family.

lessons.title: Space Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about space learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Space' display summarising planets, astronauts, and rocket launch learning.
key_questions: What have we learned about space?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about space with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: 'ch', 'sh', 'th' Digraphs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read words using the digraphs learned so far.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations: word-building with all digraphs, reading cards, simple sentence reading (e.g. 'this is a shop').
key_questions: Can you build and read this word?

differentiation.support: Build/read simple digraph words with support
differentiation.extension: Read sentences with multiple digraphs independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Finalise week 19 digraph phonics tracker for 'ch', 'sh', 'th'.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all digraphs learned with a reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading words with digraphs over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting Back, Size Order, Shape
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting backwards, size-ordering, and shape skills learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting backwards from 10, ordering planets by size, rocket shape design recap.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting backwards over the weekend.

lessons.title: Space Celebration Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to combine movement, song, and craft in a class performance.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance combining the space song and astronaut movements, with rockets displayed as a 'launch pad'.
resources_needed: Craft from the week, music player
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this week?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the space week.
lessons.home_link: Perform the space song for family this weekend.
